Every document valid at 2.17.0 stays valid; no `required` delta, no property added or removed. WHY: 2.17.0 admitted the SCOUT proposal only. Where the blitz-em overrides the scout the override lands in the em-size-review, so the admitted path reached the OVERTURNED size -- example-store-repo-fb measured it on 2026-09-11-drive-general-plaintext-regrowth-enforced-prune.md, whose trail `.sizing.md` says XS and opens "Already fully done.", and whose plan exists only because the blitz-em read the disk, found 112MB across 133 files against an audited 5.2MB, and raised it to S. A reader following the provenance link to ask what this was sized as gets the proposal that was overturned, stated confidently, with nothing saying it was. The common case was already fine; the OVERRIDDEN case is the one provenance earns its keep in. Reported by claude-klabauter-1e. AMEND-IN-PLACE WAS ATTEMPTED AND IS NOT AVAILABLE, recorded so the next author does not retry it: 2.17.0 is not yet vendored (claude-klabauter still mirrors 2.16.0), so folding this in under the same number would have cost one hold instead of two -- but `test_schema_shape_hash_matches_pin` compares the pinned shape-hash unconditionally, and a shape that moves under a version that does not is exactly the b6baf9e1 defect that gate exists to catch. The saving was real and the gate is worth more than it. WHICH FILE WINS is in the field description, not here and not in the pattern: a regex cannot express "prefer the review when one exists", and both files are openable, so the rule has to be written where an author reads it. NOT DONE HERE, and the better fix: have the wave emit a real sizing object into the run trail now that `coordinator-doc-new --type sizing-object` no longer refuses without --title, which would make both trail-markdown branches a fallback nobody normally takes. The object belongs in the trail and NOT in `state/sizings/`, for 2.17.0's own reason below -- a fleet routing-lobby record per baton a wave sizes. Two independent plan-authors refused to write a satisfying value and were right to: the only admitted alternatives were a sizing object that does not exist (minting one is the sizer's act and would invent an estimate) and a KR that does not serve the plan, which this field's own description forbids -- provenance is a LINK a reader can open and compare against, never an assertion. The trail's `.sizing.md` IS such a link. WIDENED RATHER THAN RELOCATED, on claude-klabauter-1e's recommendation: having the workflow write blitz sizings to `state/sizings/<id>.yaml` would mint a fleet routing-lobby record with a deliverable_id join for every baton a wave sizes -- hundreds of lobby entries for what is a scout's size review. The two fixes are exclusive; relocating would make this widen pointless. NOT ADMITTED, and held deliberately rather than overlooked: `state/handoffs/.+\.md`. Three of those four failing plans point at their baton record, and admitting it would make the field satisfiable by every plan that has a baton -- the bar would stop meaning 'someone sized this' and start meaning 'this plan came from somewhere'. That is a change to what the bar MEANS rather than a mechanical widen, and it is a PM ruling. Where the blitz-em overrides the scout, the override lands in the em-size-review and the admitted path reached the overturned proposal -- example-store-repo-fb measured it on 2026-09-11-drive-general-plaintext-regrowth-enforced-prune.md, whose trail `.sizing.md` opens 'Already fully done.' and whose plan exists because the blitz-em read the disk, found 112MB across 133 files against an audited 5.2MB, and raised XS to S. PRIOR: 2.13.0 -> 2.14.0 gives gated-brightline close-out evidence a declared home and widens `exit_criterion_met.promotion` onto its attested vocabulary. (1) `gated_exit_criteria[].items` gains an OPTIONAL `evidence` string, bounded at 1024. The light-row rationale in that field's description forbids a falsifier APPARATUS per brightline -- per-item spawn amplification -- which one optional string does not reach, at zero spawns. This was already owed inside this repo, independent of any sibling's ask: `coordinator/templates/plans/plan.md.tmpl`'s close-out step instructs the EM to write "gated_exit_criteria rows carrying close-out evidence and flipping met: true" against a schema that rejected every spelling of it. Two independently-authored corpora (claude-klabauter, example-game-repo) converged on `evidence` / `met_evidence` / `closeout_evidence` / `close_out_evidence` / `close_out` finding the absent slot; `evidence` is the admitted spelling and the rest retag to it. (2) NO equivalent key on `exit_criterion_met` or `prime_exit_criterion` -- RULED, not overlooked, and recorded as a NEGATIVE-SPEC on both descriptions so the next author does not re-invent it. `falsifier_output` / `falsifier_verdict` / `prose` / `reason` already ARE the close-out record; a fifth key would be a second home for it, and a close-out key on the plan-time `prime_exit_criterion` object lands on the wrong half of an existing plan-time/close-out pair. (3) `promotion` gains `promoted` and `already-in-suite`. The 2.9.0 note held that enum to attested vocabulary and named its own release condition -- "a plan whose falsifier promoted in full has no attested value here yet". It does now: five independently-authored attestations in claude-klabauter (three `promoted`, one `full`, one `already-in-suite`). This is that observation arriving, not a widen on spec. `full` is REFUSED as a duplicate spelling of `promoted` and retags to it; `already-in-suite` is admitted on its own because it records a fact neither prior value carries -- the falsifier was a standing test before the plan, so nothing graduated. `promoted_to` widens to cover `promoted` and is never null. nested-field-additive BUNDLED with enum-value-additive; both are unconditionally holding on the `x-schema-version` axis with no declared-tolerance carve-out available to either, so the recorded class understates no hold. This is the sole live hold on this file. UNCONDITIONALLY HOLDING on its own reason, not stacked on a now-discharged hold: 2.9.0/2.10.0 are DISCHARGED per cross-repo/archive/2026-08-29-claude-klabauter-em-the-schema-hold-lifts-and-nine-more-answers.md, so this bump inherits no live hold from them. It is `major`, which is unconditionally holding on the x-schema-version axis regardless of any prior discharge (docs/wiki/schema-version-gate.md) — merge-to-main and production emit are held until claude-klabauter re-vendors. Landing this row is a default-on advisory warning on every plan write until claude-klabauter re-vendors — recorded here as an accepted cost, not a defect. LIVE DRIFT (unrelated to this bump, carried forward from 2.11.0/2.12.0, not yet re-vendored): `grouping_approvals`/`$defs.grouping_approval_block` and `exit_criterion_met`'s promotion fields (`promotion`/`promotion_reason`/`promoted_to`). description: Plan frontmatter schema. The active-execution value is 'executing', NOT the intuitive 'execution'. 'implemented' means work is done on the working branch — whether it merged to main is tracked in completion log + handoff deployment_state, NOT here.

author.description: Agent or person who authored this plan.

status.description: Lifecycle state. Common slip: active-execution value is 'executing', NOT 'execution'. 'landed' sits between 'executing' and 'implemented': every chunk's code is on the branch, but not every spine row has reached a disposition yet. It is NOT terminal — a plan in 'landed' still has outstanding row-level work to close out before it can move to 'implemented'.

branch.description: Working branch this plan is being executed on.

source.description: Origin reference (e.g. a handoff slug, memo path, or external prompt).

superseded_by.description: Path or slug of the plan that supersedes this one.

scope_mode.description: Planning posture (e.g. 'architecture', 'implementation', 'spike', 'spec-dispatch' — the S-lane posture routed from coordinator:sizing: a light plan artifact scaffolded then dispatched, skipping the Opus plan review).

problem_set.description: Ratified problem-set slug or inline statement (from /shape).

predecessor_handoff.description: The handoff that spawned this plan (distinct from parent_plan). Nullable, for the same reason sizing_object is: an explicit null is the sanctioned 'this plan has no resolvable predecessor handoff' answer — a forced declaration rather than an omission, which is what makes the absence checkable. Written with an inline reason naming why (target never authored, or archived-then-pruned). 42 rows were set this way on 2026-08-14; the disposition ledger is state/audits/2026-08-13-predecessor-handoff-fk-disposition.md. A non-null value is expected to resolve on disk, literally or archive-relative — the FK is archive-agnostic by design and readers resolve archive-relative (docs/decisions/DR-159-predecessor-handoff-fk-is-archive-agnostic-by-design.md), so a value resolving only under archive/ is correct, not broken. Referential integrity is enforced by coordinator/tests/test_archive_handoff_referrer_guard.py.

prerequisite_of.description: Downstream plan(s) that depend on this plan completing first.

source_memo.description: Cross-repo memo(s) that initiated this plan. May be a single path or a list.

scope.description: In-scope items for this plan (list-of-string preferred; legacy string values accepted).

agent_sessions.description: Sessions that executed this plan. Runtime-appended by append-plan-session.sh after a successful plan claim (execute-plan Phase 1.5 Step 0); NOT scaffolded onto new plans. Each entry is the encoded string "<session_id>|<status>|<created_at>": session_id is UUID-shaped (contains no '|'); status is an OPEN string ('working' at the Phase-0 fire point, not a closed enum); created_at is ISO-8601 UTC. All three fields are non-empty at write time — consumers must NOT use `IFS='|' read -ra` if a future field could be empty (read -ra silently drops trailing empty fields). Append-only: never rewrite or reorder peer entries.

deliverable_id.description: Durable deliverable join key. Minted once at the earliest artifact and carried verbatim by every downstream artifact. dlv-<stub_id> for roadmap-stub origins; dlv-<slug>-<6hex> for standalone plan origins. Cross-field rule enforces 'dlv-' prefix when non-null. Null for pre-backfill plans. Spec backlink: claude-klabauter:pln-fleet-deliverable-spine-identity-and-facets-2b331c § D1

sizing_object.description: FK to the sizing-object (state/sizings/<id>.yaml) that routed this plan through coordinator:sizing. Optional and nullable in this schema; the requirement is enforced READ-SIDE in claude-klabauter (coordinator_core/ops/assert_plan_sizing_citation.py), never here. A plan created on/after 2026-08-06 must carry EITHER a resolving state/sizings/<id>.yaml path OR an explicit null — explicit null is the sanctioned 'no sizing object' answer, a forced declaration rather than a bypass, which is what makes the absence checkable at all. Plans created before that cutoff are permanently exempt and must NOT be backfilled: the large majority of the on-disk corpus predates the convention, and requiring it of them would invalidate the corpus. When present, the referenced file is expected to resolve on disk. Frontmatter-only: this field is never read from plan BODY prose, and no check compares its value against the plan's problem restatement — a body-scanning or intent-matching variant is out of scope by design (it fires on a plan that legitimately documents an absent or reworded citation). Bilaterally mirrored with claude-klabauter's vendored copy; originating request: state/memo-outbox/sent/plan-sizing-citation-unenforced-at-write-time.md.

plan_id.description: Stable non-path plan identity (pln-<slug>-<6hex>). Minted by coordinator-doc-new at plan creation time. Allows the board to join on a stable key independent of file path/rename. Distinct from deliverable_id (which spans the full deliverable chain). Spec backlink: claude-klabauter:pln-fleet-deliverable-spine-identity-and-facets-2b331c § D3

initiative.description: FK to the initiative entity (state/initiatives/<id>.yaml). Nullable — not all work belongs to a named initiative. Cross-field rule enforces non-empty string when non-null. Spec backlink: claude-klabauter:pln-fleet-deliverable-spine-identity-and-facets-2b331c § D2

caption.description: One-sentence business-legible outcome line. NOT an engineering title or filename — authored for CEO-board legibility. Optional; authored at creation time.

status_reason.description: Free-text one-liner explaining the current plan status (e.g. 'deferred — blocked on cockpit reader-first gate'). Optional authored field; carried into the cockpit emission as a product-legibility facet.

owner.description: Authoring workstream or EM identifier. Nullable; carried forward from the earliest artifact for the deliverable.

suggested_priority.description: Advisory execution-priority signal an EM may attach to this plan at authoring time. Optional (not nullable — absence already covers 'no suggestion'; a redundant null representation was reviewed out, see Finding 4 / review-integrator). Enum is the priority-ledger domain (priority-ledger.schema.json's urgent|high|medium|low|none) MINUS 'none' — an EM has no reason to author an explicit clear; absence of the field already covers that case. Advisory only: the PM-owned priority ledger (state/priority-ledger/) is the authoritative tier and lives on a deliberately separate surface — this field never overrides it, and that separation (not memory) is what keeps 'advisory never overrides authoritative' structural. Do NOT add a pm_priority field to this frontmatter to compensate; the tier split is the point. NEGATIVE-SPEC: no inherited_from / priority_predecessor field is permitted on this frontmatter either — priority does not chain plan-to-plan. No backfill of pre-existing plans, consistent with the handoff schema's origin_* no-backfill policy.

provisional_until.description: Expiry date (YYYY-MM-DD) for a decision this plan stages but does not yet execute — e.g. a ratification, a second stage of a two-stage rollout, or a hold pending a future condition. `revisit_by` is an accepted synonym key (same semantics, same format); a plan carries one or the other, never both. Read by the outstanding-provisional-decisions ceremony check (`coordinator/docs/wiki/provisional-decision-expiry.md`) against every non-terminal-status plan (`status` not in implemented/deferred/abandoned/superseded) — a date on or before today with the plan still non-terminal is surfaced as expired. Motivating case: the 2026-07-13 adopt spec's stage-2 ratification sat unexecuted for 13 days with nothing tracking that it was owed (archive/specs/2026-07/2026-07-13-doe-auto-reconcile-adopt.md). Optional; null/absent for plans that stage no provisional decision. Spec backlink: pln-push-side-write-discipline-for-05c30d § D1b.

revisit_by.description: Synonym key for `provisional_until` — same semantics, same format, same consumer. Use whichever name reads more naturally at the call site (`revisit_by` for a park_note-style hold; `provisional_until` for a staged-decision expiry); a plan sets at most one of the two. See `provisional_until` for the full description.

tasks.description: NOT a frontmatter key — the ## Tasks task-spine lives BODY-RESIDENT in a single fenced ```yaml plan-tasks``` code block directly under the ## Tasks heading (parser-locate rule: exactly one such block; zero or >1 is a defined error). This 'tasks' property exists to WIRE the per-row shape (schemas/plan-tasks.schema.json) into the plan schema family for validators that parse the fenced block's YAML list and want the item schema, per the canonical body-resident-machine-block pattern (docs/wiki/canonical-artifact-shapes.md § Addressable-Section Convention, rule 4 — cf. the ## Session Ledger precedent in handoffs). Full authoring contract: docs/wiki/writing-plans.md § Machine-Parseable Task Spine. Spec backlink: pln-full-coverage-planning-posture-bca96f § C1.

execution_authorized_by.description: The PM/session that authorized execution. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note), mirrored from handoff.schema.json's identically-named field for the plan→execute-plan Stop-hook seam. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

execution_authorized_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time of authorization. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note), mirrored from handoff.schema.json's identically-named field for the plan→execute-plan Stop-hook seam. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

execution_authorized_sha.description: git-hash-object of the plan body at authorization (the content-binding witness /pickup recomputes; schema shape-only). OPTIONAL — one of the four-field execution-authorization stamp (by/at/sha/note), mirrored from handoff.schema.json's identically-named field for the plan→execute-plan Stop-hook seam. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

execution_authorized_note.description: The verbatim PM utterance that named execution. The FOURTH field of the stamp: plan-execute-session-split.md § Pinned conventions pins the stamp as a byte-identical FOUR-field contract (by/at/sha/note); note is the self-attesting field — a stamp without a note that names execution signals the write-bar may not have been met. Do NOT drop it. OPTIONAL, mirrored from handoff.schema.json's identically-named field for the plan→execute-plan Stop-hook seam. Spec backlink: pln-first-class-execution-handoff--40a6e5 § C1

status_override_by.description: The session that overrode the completeness verdict when stamping `status: implemented`. OPTIONAL — one of the three-field override stamp (by/reason/at), written ONLY by `plan-status-transition stamp-implemented --override-reason`. Negative-spec: this stamp records an override of the SPINE/AC completeness verdict only; it never relaxes the live-foreign-holder refusal, which still runs unchanged. Supersedes the unschema'd hand-edit route (`status_stamped_by: EM-manual`, `status_stamped_by_hand`) that improvised two different field spellings across two repos because the engine offered no sanctioned path when it declined. Spec backlink: claude-klabauter:cross-repo/archive/2026-08-10-example-retrieval-repo-em-close-out-stamps-implemented-without-reading-the-ac-table.md

status_override_reason.description: The verbatim operator reason for overriding the completeness verdict. REQUIRED by the op whenever an override is taken — `--override-reason` refuses empty text, so a bare force with no stated cause cannot reach disk. OPTIONAL here in shape terms (absent on every non-override plan). One of the three-field override stamp (by/reason/at).

status_override_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time of the completeness-verdict override. OPTIONAL — one of the three-field override stamp (by/reason/at), written in the same locked_rmw mutate closure as the status flip it accompanies, so the stamp and the flip cannot diverge.

review_signals.description: Selects which reviewers this plan needs, forward — distinct from `reviewer`, which records who already approved it, backward. Values are not enumerated here by design — the vocabulary is `coordinator/contract/review-signals.json`, and membership is enforced by the contract's parity test plus the frontmatter write guard where a coordinator engine is installed.

review_verified_by.description: The session that recorded a code-review pass over the work this plan delivered. OPTIONAL — one of the three-field review attest (by/at/findings), written ONLY by `plan-status-transition` alongside a terminal `status: implemented`, in the same locked_rmw mutate closure as the flip it accompanies, so the attest and the status cannot diverge. Negative-spec: this is an attest, not a status — absence means no code review was recorded, never that a review failed, and nothing gates a close-out on it. Spec backlink: pln-a-plan-s-status-advances-itsel-fb8bf2 § C1(c).

review_verified_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time of the code-review pass. OPTIONAL — one of the three-field review attest (by/at/findings).

review_verified_findings.description: Path to the review-trail record the pass produced, e.g. `state/review-trail/findings/<date>-<slug>.md`. OPTIONAL — one of the three-field review attest (by/at/findings). A path, never a count: a count is a lossy copy of a record that already exists on disk and drifts from it. This value is also the attest's IDEMPOTENCE KEY — a re-run of the same wrap with an unchanged path writes nothing, while a genuine second review after fixes produces a new path and writes a fresh attest.

mise_prepped_by.description: The session that recorded a passing mise-prep gate run over this plan. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field mise-prep attest (`mise_prepped_by`/`_at`/`_sha`/`_findings`): one stamp, all four written together or none. Required-together is a cross-field rule in claude-klabauter's coordinator_core/frontmatter/schema_validate.py; JSON Schema cannot express it and this file is not the enforcement point. Stamped BESIDE `status`, never added to it. Written only by claude-klabauter's `plan.stamp_prepped`, which refuses unless `plan.prep_gate` passes. THE PREDICATE IS A RECOMPUTED `mise_prepped_sha`, NEVER THE PRESENCE OF THIS FIELD — a present stamp over a mismatched body is STALE, not absent, and the two route to different repairs. NEGATIVE-SPEC: an attest, not a status — absence means no mise-prep gate run was recorded, never that one failed. Contract: coordinator/docs/wiki/mise-prepped-attest.md. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-09-07-mise-prepped-attest.md § C1

mise_prepped_at.description: ISO 8601 date-time of the gate run. Deliberately a bare string with no `format: date-time`, byte-identical to `execution_authorized_at` and `review_verified_at` — the corpus's date handling is lenient by contract (`_coerce_dates_to_strings`) and a format assertion here would fail records the validator is required to accept. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field mise-prep attest (`mise_prepped_by`/`_at`/`_sha`/`_findings`): one stamp, all four written together or none. NEGATIVE-SPEC: an attest, not a status — absence means no mise-prep gate run was recorded, never that one failed. It is a timestamp, never a freshness predicate. Contract: coordinator/docs/wiki/mise-prepped-attest.md. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-09-07-mise-prepped-attest.md § C1

mise_prepped_sha.description: git-hash-object of the plan BODY at stamp time — `coordinator_core/frontmatter/primitives.py :: canonical_body_sha(file_text)` = `git_blob_sha1(frontmatter_body_text(file_text))`, everything below the second `---` delimiter. FRONTMATTER IS EXCLUDED BY DESIGN, which is what lets the stamp survive its own write and the `status` flips that follow it. Not `blitz_land :: _git_blob_sha`, which hashes the whole file. Schema shape-only: this file asserts the hex shape and nothing about the value. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field mise-prep attest (`mise_prepped_by`/`_at`/`_sha`/`_findings`): one stamp, all four written together or none. THE PREDICATE IS A RECOMPUTED VALUE OF THIS FIELD, NEVER THE PRESENCE OF THE STAMP — a mismatch is STALE, not absent, and stale re-gates where absent stamps. NEGATIVE-SPEC: an attest, not a status — absence means no mise-prep gate run was recorded, never that one failed. Contract: coordinator/docs/wiki/mise-prepped-attest.md. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-09-07-mise-prepped-attest.md § C1

mise_prepped_findings.description: The spine row ids the gate WITHHELD at stamp time — rows an `external_gate` carrying `requires: landed-work` blocks while the plan still certifies. IDS, NOT PROSE AND NOT A COUNT: they point into the plan's own `## Tasks` spine, which is the record. `mise_prepped_findings: []` is a DECLARED-EMPTY and structurally different from an absent key — the same distinction `writes: []` draws. Its named reader is the aggregate execution baton's roll-up (coordinator/docs/wiki/aggregate-execution-baton.md), which builds the withheld list a partial fire must name. OPTIONAL — one of the four-field mise-prep attest (`mise_prepped_by`/`_at`/`_sha`/`_findings`): one stamp, all four written together or none. NEGATIVE-SPEC: an attest, not a status — absence means no mise-prep gate run was recorded, never that one failed. It is never a defect list either: `requires: commit-in-owner-repo` refuses the whole plan, and a refused plan is never stamped. Contract: coordinator/docs/wiki/mise-prepped-attest.md. Spec backlink: docs/plans/2026-09-07-mise-prepped-attest.md § C1

census.description: OPTIONAL for schema validity, REQUIRED-AS-A-KEY by the mise-prep authoring bar: every counted premise this plan rests on, as the command that produced the count and the answer it gave, so a count can be RE-ASKED of HEAD at fire time instead of trusted. A plan that rests on no counted premise declares `census: []` — a DECLARED-EMPTY, structurally different from an absent key, exactly as `writes: []` is in plan-tasks.schema.json. NEGATIVE SPEC: not a place for a count the spine already declares (`writes:` is that record); not close-out evidence (`exit_criterion_met` is); nothing runs these commands at validation time — re-running is fire-time work for the runner. NOT census-document.schema.json, a different artifact wearing the same word: that is the conversion-census SIDECAR DOCUMENT, with its own file and row shape and no relation to this key. Checked by coordinator/bin/mise-prep-gate.py; authoring bar: coordinator/docs/wiki/mise-prepped-authoring-bar.md § Census.

question.description: What was counted, in one line — the question a fire-time re-run is asking again. Reader-facing; the machine-checkable half is `command`/`result`.

command.description: The exact command that produced `result`, re-runnable as written. A description of how the count was obtained does not satisfy this field — a driver has to be able to run it without reconstructing it. Never run at validation time.

result.description: What `command` answered, verbatim enough to diff a re-run against. A bare integer is fine; so is a short line of output. A paraphrase defeats the field.

ref.description: OPTIONAL — the tree state `command` was run against (a sha, a date, or `HEAD`). Absence is not a defect: a re-run diffs against `result` whether or not the original ref is named, and this only says WHEN drift began, never THAT it did.

prime_exit_criterion.description: The plan-level falsifiable exit criterion — 'what is true of the tree when this plan has delivered', outcome-shaped per goal.schema.json's vocabulary. Deliberately NO `source`/provenance enum: a self-declared provenance flag is the unfalsifiable shape this plan (pln-plan-goal-as-a-first-class-exit-criterion) exists to remove. Provenance is instead `derived_from`, a LINK a reader can open and compare against, never an assertion. PROPORTIONALITY (enforced READ-SIDE, the same locus as `sizing_object`'s own cross-document requirement, never structurally in this file because `estimate.tshirt` lives in the external sizing-object document, not here): `falsifier` is REQUIRED only when the plan's `sizing_object` resolves to `estimate.tshirt` M/L/XL. At size S (spec-dispatch posture) a plan carries `statement`+`derived_from` only, no falsifier. XS never scaffolds a plan at all, so this object never appears. XXL routes to prime-exit-criterion-setting/roadmap, not a single plan; its obligation is discharged per-child-plan. The size carve-out keys ONLY on `estimate.tshirt` through `sizing_object` — never on an EM-set field, and never on plain field optionality: the shape below still marks `falsifier` absent from THIS object's own `required` array (JSON Schema cannot condition on a sibling document's content), but a plan sized M+ with no `falsifier` and no `falsifier_exemption` fails the read-side check even though it validates here. Do not read the schema-level optionality as the plan's own gate. NEGATIVE-SPEC — NO CLOSE-OUT KEY OF ANY SPELLING BELONGS ON THIS OBJECT. It is authored before the work exists; evidence can only be known after it. Every plan-time field here has its paired close-out field on `exit_criterion_met` (`falsifier.how`/`falsifier_output`, `falsifier.expected_when_true`/`falsifier_verdict`), and an `evidence`-class key written here is that record landing on the wrong half of the pair — it retags to `exit_criterion_met.prose` or `.falsifier_output`, never to a new key on either object.

statement.description: One falsifiable sentence naming what is true of the tree when this plan has delivered. Outcome-shaped (a measurable change in behaviour or state), never output-shaped (a deliverable produced, a task list wearing this field's clothes).

derived_from.description: Provenance BY LINK, not by self-declaration: a path to the sizing object that routed this plan (`state/sizings/<id>.yaml`, same shape as this schema's own top-level `sizing_object` field) or a key-result reference (`<goal_id>#kr-<kr-id>`, e.g. `goal-shipping-velocity#kr-throughput`) naming a KR in `state/goals/*.yaml` this plan serves — `<goal_id>` is the target goal's `id` field and `<kr-id>` is that goal's `key_results[].id` (goal.schema.json), never an array index, exactly like `kr-suggestion.schema.json`'s own `goal_id`/`kr_id` anchors. Openable and comparable against `statement` — the corpus-existing `intent`/`intent_source` fields already carry what this points at; no new sizing-object field was added for it. A plan links to a KR it serves without the KR itself gaining a falsifier or an AC-table binding — one KR spans several plans, so this is a pointer, never a merge of the two documents. WHICH TRAIL FILE, when a blitz wave authored the plan: the wave's `state/plan-blitz/<run>/wave-<n>.em-size-review.md` WHENEVER ONE EXISTS, and the baton's `<baton>.sizing.md` only when it does not. The `.sizing.md` is the SCOUT's proposal and the em-size-review is the finalised size; where the blitz-em overrode the scout, the scout's file states the size and the reasoning that were overturned, in its opening lines, with nothing in it saying so. Both are openable, so a reader who follows the wrong one gets a confident answer that is the opposite of this plan's premise. A pattern cannot express 'prefer the review when one exists'; this sentence is where that rule lives.

falsifier.description: The plan-time-authored observation distinguishing the prime exit criterion being true from false, with its baseline captured BEFORE any work — authored by someone with no stake yet in the answer. This is NOT a typed cell and is NOT bound to the AC table: it is one observation per plan, EM-chosen free form (a command, a query, a measurement, a named manual observation), judged by a human reading the re-run against a stated pass condition, never a script's exit code or a `grep:`/`pytest:`/`sh:` typed cell. It is NOT the retired acceptance oracle: it is categorically different on five axes (cardinality, typing, chooser, judge, target artifact); see `docs/wiki/coordinator-tripwires/tripwire-registry/acceptance-oracle-gate-retired.md` for the retired mechanism this must not be reshaped back into, and do not 'improve' this field into a typed cell or delete it as a revival of that retirement. Mutually exclusive with `falsifier_exemption` — a prime exit criterion carries at most one of the two.

how.description: The observation that distinguishes the prime exit criterion being true from false. Form is the EM's choice — a command, a query, a measurement, a named manual observation. Bounded at 4096 chars: this lands raw in the plan's YAML frontmatter, where an unbounded payload is a corpus hazard and the frontmatter validator is lenient about coercions. Output over the bound means the falsifier is too wide, never that the record should be truncated — narrow the observation (a count, a filtered line set).

baseline_output.description: The raw output of `how`, run against HEAD before any work. Must show the prime exit criterion is currently FALSE — a baseline that already passes means the criterion is mis-stated, the work is already done, or the falsifier does not measure the criterion, all of which are worth catching at plan time. Bounded at 4096 chars: this lands raw in the plan's YAML frontmatter, where an unbounded payload is a corpus hazard and the frontmatter validator is lenient about coercions. Output over the bound means the falsifier is too wide, never that the record should be truncated — narrow the observation (a count, a filtered line set).

promoted_to.description: The test path this falsifier graduated into when it was executable and deterministic enough to become a standing regression pin. Promotion is REAL but never a gate: an unpromotable falsifier (a manual observation, a measurement against a live index) is not a lesser falsifier, and making promotability a precondition for the stamp would push EMs to choose falsifiers for their promotability rather than their discrimination. Mutually exclusive with `promotion`.

promotion.description: The recorded NON-promotion, for a falsifier that cannot graduate into the suite. Held to a single spelling so the field cannot become a free-text status. Requires `promotion_reason`. Mutually exclusive with `promoted_to`.

promotion_reason.description: Why this falsifier does not promote — a manual observation, a measurement against a live index, a one-shot migration check. Close-out accepts this and stamps; the reason is for a later reader deciding whether promotion became possible since.

baseline_ref.description: Where the baseline was taken (a commit sha). One falsifier per plan, one baseline_ref — never one per AC row, which would be per-item git-spawn amplification.

expected_when_true.description: What `how`'s observation yields WHEN the prime exit criterion is TRUE — the stated pass condition the close-out re-run is judged against. Makes the falsifier a discriminating observation, not a blob to diff: a re-run output is judged by whether it matches this shape/content, never by whether it merely differs from `baseline_output`. A non-null delta from baseline that still does not match `expected_when_true` is a criterion that is still false, differently. Bounded at 4096 chars for the same corpus-hazard reason as `how`/`baseline_output`.

falsifier_exemption.description: The NAMED escape hatch for an M+ prime exit criterion genuinely un-falsifiable-by-observation — pure doctrine/schema edits where 'run it and watch it fail' is contrived (this plan is itself in that class; see its own § This plan's own falsifier). Distinct from, and never a substitute for, the size carve-out: the size carve-out is a rule about which PLANS the instrument suits (keyed on `estimate.tshirt`), this is a rule about which M+ CRITERIA resist any instrument, and the two do not merge — a plan cannot claim exemption from `falsifier` by pointing at its size, nor claim the size carve-out by pointing at this exemption. NEVER `falsifier: optional`: this object exists precisely so optionality is never reopened as the way out. Mutually exclusive with `falsifier`.

class.description: The one admitted class, held to a single spelling so a later reader cannot widen it by inventing new class strings. Covers only work with no runtime behaviour to observe — doctrine prose, schema/contract shape edits with no executable surface a `how` could measure.

admission.description: The written admission test: a non-empty statement that (1) names why no baseline-red observation exists for this specific prime exit criterion, (2) confirms the change is doctrine/schema/contract-shaped with no runtime behaviour a falsifier could observe, and (3) is written by someone who first tried and failed to draft a `falsifier`, not someone who skipped the attempt. An admission that could be copy-pasted onto any plan without editing is not admissible — it must speak to THIS criterion.

gated_exit_criteria.description: The fleet brightlines, discharged as a machine-readable field on the plan artifact the executor holds rather than remembered from a doctrine page. Scaffolded in full by `coordinator/templates/plans/plan.md.tmpl`; a row is never deleted because it seems inapplicable, its `statement` is narrowed instead. Deliberately NOT a repeated `prime_exit_criterion`-shaped object: a full falsifier per brightline is per-item spawn amplification for a check that is almost always a direct read, so this stays a light three-field row and `prime_exit_criterion.falsifier` stays the one-per-plan heavy instrument. Deliberately NOT an `## Acceptance Criteria` table row either — that table is optional, reviewer-facing prose and is never mechanically gated, so a brightline landed there would be present but not gated, which is the exact failure this field exists to close.

brightline.description: A fixed slug. The enum is the mechanism: an ad-hoc slug is how a brightline becomes a freehand row nothing gates. A new brightline is a plan chunk that extends this enum and the template together, never a plan-local addition.

statement.description: Authored at plan-write time: what evidence at close-out would show this brightline held for THIS plan's delivered work. Same falsifiable-sentence discipline as `prime_exit_criterion.statement`, scoped to one brightline. `work-vs-question-ratio` is discharged by naming, per function, corpus-scale value, or durable artifact the plan introduces, the bounded question it answers — an act, never the bare disposition "proportionate". A doc-only plan does NOT discharge this row vacuously on "no executable code, nothing to justify": the unit a documentation plan introduces is the artifact — a wiki page, a decision record, a schema row, a discharge marker — and each one is enumerated and answered separately, because artifact-count-to-question is the imbalance this class of plan actually has. It is the per-unit row: `work-proportionate-to-question` weighs the delivered work AS A WHOLE against the size of the question, so a statement that discharges one must not discharge the other. `right-not-merely-working` is discharged by naming, per surface delivered, the simpler or cheaper shape considered and rejected and why the delivered one is right — never portability, which stays `multi-os-first-class`'s row.

met.description: Starts `false` and is flipped only by the session writing `exit_criterion_met` — never pre-set `true` at authoring time. An unmet brightline blocks `implemented` the same way an unresolved prime exit criterion does, on that same close-out path; there is deliberately no second enforcement path.

evidence.description: OPTIONAL, written at close-out beside the `met` flip: what was actually observed that shows this brightline's `statement` held. `statement` is the plan-time question, this is the answer — proof text never belongs in `statement`, and a row is never stripped of a recorded observation to satisfy the validator. Deliberately a bare string and not a `falsifier`-shaped object: the light-row rationale in this field's own description forbids a per-brightline falsifier APPARATUS (per-item spawn amplification for a check that is almost always a direct read), which one optional string does not reach — it costs zero spawns. Bounded at 1024 for the same reason `exit_criterion_met.falsifier_output` is bounded at 4096, scaled to a five-row array: this lands raw in the plan's YAML frontmatter and an unbounded payload is a corpus hazard. Over the bound means the observation is too wide, never that the record should be truncated — narrow it to a count or a filtered line set. A row with `met: true` and no `evidence` is valid; the flip is the gate, this is the receipt.

exit_criterion_met.description: Written once, at close-out, by the EM — the assertion half of the prime-exit-criterion pair. `asserted: false` is a legitimate, first-class outcome (the plan is Phase-5-halted, not `implemented`); what is forbidden is the field's absence. Not bound to the AC table — see `prime_exit_criterion.falsifier`'s description for the acceptance-oracle distinction, which applies identically here. NEGATIVE-SPEC — THIS OBJECT TAKES NO `evidence`-CLASS KEY, and its absence is a ruling, not an oversight: `falsifier_output` is the raw observation, `falsifier_verdict` is its reading, `prose` is the EM's sentence tying the two to the criterion, and `reason` carries a `false` assertion's remainder. Those four ARE the close-out record. An invented `evidence` / `met_evidence` / `closeout_evidence` / `close_out_evidence` / `close_out` key retags into them — raw output to `falsifier_output`, narrative to `prose` — and is never added here as a fifth home for a record four fields already hold. The optional `evidence` string on `gated_exit_criteria[]` is NOT a precedent for one here: that row had no evidence field at all, this object has four.

asserted.description: Whether HEAD now satisfies `prime_exit_criterion.statement`. `false` is legitimate and takes `reason`; it is never omitted in place of a `false` value.

asserted_by.description: The session id of the EM that made the assertion. Names WHO looked, so an assertion is attributable rather than anonymous — route-c's stamp was made in good faith by an EM who had genuinely looked, and attribution is what lets a later reader ask them what they saw.

asserted_at.description: ISO-8601 date the assertion was made. Dates the observation, so a re-run against a much later HEAD is visibly not the same evidence.

falsifier_output.description: The SAME observation (`prime_exit_criterion.falsifier.how`) re-run against HEAD, raw. Judged against `prime_exit_criterion.falsifier.expected_when_true`, never against `baseline_output` alone — a changed output that still does not match `expected_when_true` is a criterion that is still false, differently, and unchanged output fails the same check without needing a separate rule. Bounded at 4096 chars: this lands raw in the plan's YAML frontmatter, where an unbounded payload is a corpus hazard and the frontmatter validator is lenient about coercions. Output over the bound means the falsifier is too wide, never that the record should be truncated — narrow the observation (a count, a filtered line set).

falsifier_verdict.description: The re-run's verdict: whether `falsifier_output` matches `prime_exit_criterion.falsifier.expected_when_true`. The gate refuses the stamp unless this is `pass`. Written beside `falsifier_output`, never inferred by a downstream reader from the raw output alone.

prose.description: The EM's own sentence tying the falsifier_output verdict to the prime exit criterion. The verdict is the evidence; this is the signature, not a substitute for it — an assertion with no falsifier output beside it is a checkbox.

reason.description: REQUIRED when `asserted: false`. What is not true of HEAD yet, and where the remainder is routed.

promotion.description: Whether the falsifier (`prime_exit_criterion.falsifier`) graduated into the standing test suite at close-out. NOT A SECOND HOME for `prime_exit_criterion.falsifier.promotion` -- that field is a PLAN-TIME up-front declaration (const "not-applicable" only, authored before the work exists, for a falsifier known in advance to resist graduation), while this field is the CLOSE-OUT record of what actually happened, which can only be known after execution and is why "partial" exists only here. Same plan-time/close-out pairing this schema already uses for `falsifier.how`/`exit_criterion_met.falsifier_output` and `falsifier.expected_when_true`/`exit_criterion_met.falsifier_verdict` -- one field authored before the work, its paired field recording the outcome after. NEGATIVE-SPEC: records the falsifier's fate, never the plan's own status -- `asserted` remains the sole authority on whether the exit criterion was met. "not-applicable" is the falsifier staying a standalone re-run, never entering the suite; "partial" is some but not all of it graduating; "promoted" is all of it graduating; "already-in-suite" is the falsifier having been a standing test BEFORE the plan, so nothing graduated -- a distinct fact from both a full promotion and a not-applicable one, and the reason it is its own value rather than folded into either. Still held to the observed vocabulary only -- do not widen this enum on spec. `promoted` and `already-in-suite` were admitted on attestation, not spec: five independently-authored close-outs in claude-klabauter reached for them once the prior two values could not carry the fact. `full` is NOT a member -- it was one of those attestations and it means exactly what `promoted` means; one fact takes one spelling, so `full` retags to `promoted`.

promotion_reason.description: Why the falsifier was or was not promoted into the standing suite — what graduated, what didn't, and why. Paired with `promotion`; free text rather than enumerated because the reasoning is the point.

promoted_to.description: The test path the falsifier (or the promoted portion of it) graduated into, when `promotion` is "partial" or "promoted". A path, not a description -- PAIRS WITH, never duplicates, `prime_exit_criterion.falsifier.promoted_to`: the falsifier-side field records a full a-priori graduation target chosen at plan-write time (before the work exists), this field records the actual close-out outcome, which may differ or may not be knowable until the falsifier is re-run. Not written for "already-in-suite" -- nothing graduated, so there is no graduation target; the standing test the falsifier already was belongs in `promotion_reason`. Never null: a value that is not known is the key omitted, never the key present holding null. See `promotion`'s description for the plan-time/close-out pairing pattern this follows.

grouping_approvals.description: $comment: BLOCK PRESENCE IS THE WHOLE GOVERNED/LEGACY DISCRIMINATOR. A plan's frontmatter carrying this key at all makes the plan GOVERNED; a plan with no such key is LEGACY and keeps the existing per-row `pm_approved` gate unchanged. There is deliberately NO schema_version conjunct anywhere in this discriminator — do not add one. Presence-only is not taken bare, though: a GOVERNED plan whose `grouping_approvals` block is malformed, or that lacks the grouping a closed row needs, FAILS LOUD (schema violation here, plus the hard authorization check in schema_validate.py's check_plan_tasks_grouping_approval) — it does NOT silently degrade to legacy treatment. `additionalProperties: false` and `required: ["status"]` on each block (below) are what make a malformed block a structural violation rather than something that reads as merely absent. Groupings are DERIVED from each task-spine row's `disposition` and never stored separately: do <- open/coded; spun_off <- spun_off; defer <- backlogged; ruled_out <- wont_do. Every grouping except `do` is PM-gated: `spun_off`, `defer` and `ruled_out` each need an approved block before their rows may close. NOT-YET-ENFORCED-FOR-`spun_off`: this key is declarable here, but the authorization predicate that reads it (claude-klabauter's `check_plan_tasks_grouping_approval`) does not scan `spun_off` until claude-klabauter re-vendors this file and widens its GOVERNED-leg set. Until then a `spun_off` row on a governed plan still closes with no PM turn -- declare the block, do not assume the gate. Moving a row to another plan is ratified like dropping one, because nothing leaving the corpus is not the same as nothing leaving the plan — a row spun off on the EM's own say-so lets a plan close having shipped less than it committed to, with no PM turn anywhere in the sequence. What differs between them is the ARGUMENT required, not the assent: `case_against` is asked only of `backlogged`/`wont_do`, which drop work outright; approving a move and arguing against a drop are different asks. Plan-level approval is the SUM of the block statuses, COMPUTED at read time — never stored as a fourth rollup field (a stored rollup would be a second home for a derivable truth, and the two would drift). Mirrors claude-klabauter's vendored shape in coordinator_core/frontmatter/schemas/plan-tasks.schema.json (`$defs.grouping_approval_block`) — do not diverge from that spelling. Spec backlink: pln-pm-approved-gets-falsifiable-p-00737d § C1.

grouping_approval_block.description: One grouping_approvals grouping's approval state (do | spun_off | defer | ruled_out). `pending` is the default, unapproved state. `approved` requires a non-empty `pm_utterance` (the PM's verbatim reasoning — testimonial, never backfilled/inferred) and a `digest` matching `sha256:<hex>` (a fresh recomputation over the CURRENT spine membership for this grouping — see schema_validate.py's compute_grouping_digest for the exact recipe). The `sha256:` prefix is load-bearing, never bare 40-hex hash: a membership digest names nothing in any git object store, so a bare-hex value would look like (and invite confusion with) a git object id, when the only valid operation on it is recompute-and-compare. `additionalProperties: false` plus `required: ["status"]` mean an unrecognized key or a missing `status` is a schema violation, not something that silently reads as an absent/legacy block.

approver.description: Who approved this grouping (PM identity/handle). Null while pending.

approved_at.description: Date this grouping was approved (YYYY-MM-DD). Null while pending.

pm_utterance.description: The PM's verbatim reasoning for approving this grouping. REQUIRED non-empty when status: approved (see allOf below). Never synthesized or backfilled — a grouping's assent is testimonial, not mechanically derivable from disk state.

digest.description: sha256:<hex> membership digest over the sorted set of (row id, disposition) pairs for the rows currently in this grouping, and nothing else. REQUIRED when status: approved (see allOf below). Row order, row body prose, section rendering, other frontmatter fields, and whitespace/YAML-style differences are all NOT covered.

allOf.$comment: Cross-field rule: status: approved requires non-empty pm_utterance and a well-formed digest. Presence-only / non-hard-failing at THIS schema layer — the hard truthiness/freshness check (does the digest match a FRESH recomputation? is pm_utterance non-empty, not just present?) is schema_validate.py's job (check_plan_tasks_grouping_approval), not this file's.
